angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 438,291 km at 130.83 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.6433 +/- 0.0153 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 130.83 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.63 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-154 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract): 438,291 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.65 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-154 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4097 +/- 40 K from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-154 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-154 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-154.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.652, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-154 (pscomppars): spectral type M0.0 V, from Hirano et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..127H/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, K2-154: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-154 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.21 dex, from Livingston et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-154 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.01773, from Hirano et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....155..127H/abstract)
